title: Delegation brief, v2 (coordinator -> spoke)
description: The coordinator writes every brief as JSON against this schema, then renders it with `uv run --script .claude/hooks/delegation.py render-brief <file>`. That checks the schema and the semantic rules (scope inside the agent's ownership, a unique scratch dir) and prints the prompt to hand to the Agent tool. Rendering makes every brief the same shape. See the /delegate skill and .claude/schemas/examples/brief.*.json.

agent.description: The spoke this brief is for; must be an agent in .claude/ownership.json.

issue.description: The GitHub issue this round works on, or null for untracked work (rare: file one first).

round.description: Review round, starting at 1. Omit for a one-shot task.

base_sha.description: The commit the spoke must start from. Commit contract changes before delegating: a worktree spoke branches from the coordinator's HEAD (worktree.baseRef = head), never from uncommitted work.

scratch_dir.description: This spoke's own scratch subdirectory, e.g. <scratchpad>/183-web-r2/. Never the bare scratchpad root: parallel spokes' sabotage runners collided there.

objective.description: What to produce, specific enough that success or failure is unambiguous. State goals and quality criteria, not a step-by-step procedure.

contract.description: The relevant slice of a shared interface pasted verbatim, plus any measured numbers the rubric depends on (compute them over real data first: a hand-checked example row proves nothing). null if the task needs none. The spoke sees nothing the brief doesn't contain.

scope.description: Repo-relative paths or globs this round may change. Must sit inside the agent's `owns` in .claude/ownership.json (checked). Read-only agents may scope anything.

negative.description: Explicitly out of scope: other agents' territory, forbidden actions, tempting side quests.

rubric.description: How the work is judged: the tests written first (TDD), checks that must be clean, behaviours to verify, sabotage expectations.

concurrency.description: Other rounds running right now and the files they touch, so the spoke can report a collision instead of racing it. null only if nothing else runs.

gate.description: Required shape for any round that builds or tightens an enforcement gate (a lint rule, an a11y check, grounding, a currency check). null otherwise. #90 took five review rounds because round 1 had no threat model or stopping rule.

threat_model.description: What the gate must stop, e.g. 'accidental erosion; deliberate evasion must leave a visible trace'.

blocking_definition.description: What counts as a blocking review finding, e.g. 'an ordinary accidental escape, a false positive on legitimate code, or a vacuous check'.

out_of_scope.description: Deliberate-evasion routes that become their own issues, not more rounds.
